title: Nine Inches of Wax
subtitle: 蜡烛与手工艺 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 蜡烛与手工艺（文学艺术与体育·手工艺与创造）
meta: 主题语境：蜡烛与手工艺（文学艺术与体育·手工艺与创造）　|　核心词汇：candle　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 candle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 my mother was sent to light ① a candle she could not hold, and she said the holding was the whole of the lesson. The ② candle, meaning the wax and not the flame, was nine inches tall and was lit by whoever came last; a candle, she said, is the only thing in a church that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ candle in that church had the same wick, and the ④ candle at the front, meaning the one the sexton kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever lit properly. A candle, my grandmother said, is nine parts wax and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the wax is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ candle was the whole of the vigil, meaning the night it lit and not the wax. The ⑥ candle, meaning the vigil and not any of that, is the only thing in a house that everybody watches and nobody questions; a candle, he said, is either something you light or the only word that means both a wax and a vigil. She said the vigil is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ candle had become a photograph in a report, and the report had become an argument about the wick. The ⑧ candle of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine inches and eleven years of lighting; a candle, she said, is either the one at the front or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ candle I remember is the one at the front, which was burned in 1971 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ candle, my grandmother said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being burned; every candle, she said, is a vigil that has agreed to look like a wax. She said the vigil was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 蜡烛（指那支蜡本身，与火焰相对）
C. 固定搭配：light a candle 点燃一支蜡烛
D. n. 蜡烛（指教堂里每一支）
E. n. 蜡烛（指前面那一支）
F. n. 蜡烛（抽象：它照亮的那个守夜）
G. n. 那个守夜（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a candle she could not hold
The candle, meaning the wax and not the flame
candle was the whole of the vigil
the candle had become a photograph in a report
The candle of the whole thing
A candle, my grandmother said in 1976

answers.why: light a candle 意为“点燃一支蜡烛”，1950 年母亲被派去点燃一支她握不住的蜡烛。
candle 意为“蜡烛”，指那支蜡本身而不是火焰，高九英寸，由最后走的人点上。
candle 指教堂里每一支蜡烛，每一支都是同样的烛芯。
candle 指前面那一支（教堂司事留的那一支），是唯一有人认真点过的。
candle 意为“蜡烛”，抽象指它照亮的那个守夜，父亲说 candle 就是那个守夜的全部。
candle 为抽象用法，指那个守夜本身，是屋子里人人都看着、却没人质疑的东西。
candle 意为“蜡烛”，到 1966 年这支 candle 成了报告里的一张照片。
candle 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九英寸和十一年的点燃。
candle 意为“蜡烛”，我记得的是前面那一支，1971 年烧尽，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
candle 为抽象总称，祖母说蜡烛是唯一会因为被点燃烧尽而变好的东西。
